scenario: 设计广告 CTR 预测：输入是稀疏类别 embedding + 稠密数值，要在 sub-100ms 内出预测。
scenario_en: Designing ad CTR prediction: input is sparse categorical embeddings plus dense numerics, predicted within sub-100ms.
q: CTR 模型设计的核心张力和三个关键决策是什么？
q_en: What is the core tension and three key decisions in CTR model design?
why: 核心张力是记忆（记住 user×advertiser 这类共现）vs 泛化（预测没见过的组合）；三个决策是架构、校准、多任务。
why_en: The core tension is memorization (recalling feature co-occurrences like user_id x advertiser_id) versus generalization (predicting unseen combos), and the three decisions are architecture, calibration, and multi-task learning.
diagram:
flowchart LR M["记忆
记住共现"] --- T["核心张力"] G["泛化
预测新组合"] --- T T --> D1["架构"] T --> D2["校准"] T --> D3["多任务"]
options: 核心是模型参数量 vs 学习率；三决策：数据规模、训练框架、机房选址与预算
记忆(记共现) vs 泛化(预测新组合)；三决策：架构、校准、多任务
核心是离线 AUC vs 线上延迟；三决策：特征工程、负采样、结果缓存
没有真正张力，模型堆够大就能同时拿到记忆和泛化
options_en: Core is model size vs learning rate; the three decisions are data scale, training framework, and datacenter budget.
Core tension = memorization (recall co-occurrences) vs generalization (predict new combos); three decisions = architecture, calibration, multi-task.
Core is offline AUC vs online latency; the three decisions are feature engineering, negative sampling, and result caching.
There's no real tension — just make the model big enough to get memorization and generalization together.
optionExplanations: 参数量/学习率是训练细节，不是 CTR 设计的核心张力与决策。
对；记忆 vs 泛化是主轴，架构/校准/多任务是三大设计决策。
前后端与 CTR 建模的记忆-泛化张力无关。
记忆和泛化有内在取舍，不是堆大模型就能免费兼得。
optionExplanations_en: Params/learning rate are training details, not CTR's core tension and decisions.
Correct — memorization vs generalization is the axis, with architecture/calibration/multi-task the three decisions.
Frontend/backend is unrelated to the memorization-generalization tension.
Memorization and generalization inherently trade off; a big model doesn't get both for free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，广告排序的核心预测目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions clicked, the core prediction target in ad ranking.

termDefinitions.term: memorization vs generalization / 记忆 vs 泛化
termDefinitions.meaning: 记忆=记住特征共现(user×advertiser)，泛化=预测没见过的组合，两者需在架构里平衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization recalls feature co-occurrences (user x advertiser); generalization predicts unseen combos — balanced in the architecture.

scenario: 面试官让你讲 Wide & Deep（Google 2016）怎么同时兼顾记忆和泛化。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how Wide & Deep (Google 2016) balances memorization and generalization.
q: Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧和 deep 侧各干什么？
q_en: What do the wide and deep sides of Wide & Deep each do?
why: wide 侧是线性模型，吃人工交叉特征做记忆；deep 侧是前馈 NN，吃 embedding 做泛化。两侧联合训练成一个 logistic loss。
why_en: The wide side is a linear model over raw plus manual cross features that memorizes strong co-occurrences (user_id x advertiser_id), while the deep side is a feedforward NN over dense embeddings that generalizes, jointly trained with a combined logistic loss.
diagram:
flowchart TB R["原始+人工交叉特征"] --> W["wide 线性
记忆"] E["稠密 embedding"] --> D["deep NN
泛化"] W --> J["联合 logistic loss"] D --> J
options: wide 侧线性吃人工交叉做记忆，deep 侧 NN 吃 embedding 做泛化
wide 和 deep 两侧都只做泛化，模型没有任何记忆能力
wide 侧是深层 NN 做泛化，deep 侧是线性模型做记忆，两者角色正好反过来
两侧完全独立训练、各出各的分数，最后不合并成同一个 loss
options_en: Wide is linear over manual crosses for memorization; deep is an NN over embeddings for generalization.
Both the wide and deep sides only generalize, so the model has no memorization at all.
Wide is a deep NN doing generalization and deep is a linear model doing memorization — the roles are reversed.
The two sides train fully independently, each emitting its own score, never merging into one loss.
optionExplanations: 对；wide 记忆强共现、deep 泛化新组合，联合 logistic 训练，兼顾两端。
wide 侧的人工交叉正是为记忆而设，不是没有记忆。
说反了：wide 是线性、deep 才是 NN。
两侧联合训练共享一个 loss，不是各出各的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — wide memorizes strong co-occurrences, deep generalizes new combos, jointly logistic-trained.
The wide side's manual crosses exist for memorization — it's not memoryless.
Backwards: wide is linear, deep is the NN.
The two sides jointly train on one loss, not separately.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 2016 的 CTR 架构：wide 线性记忆人工交叉，deep NN 泛化 embedding，联合训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wide & Deep (Google 2016) is a CTR architecture: a wide linear side memorizes manual crosses and a deep NN generalizes embeddings, jointly trained.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个类别特征组合成一个（如 user_id×advertiser_id），捕捉共现，Wide&Deep 里靠人工构造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross feature combines two categorical features (e.g. user_id x advertiser_id) to capture co-occurrence, hand-crafted in Wide & Deep.

scenario: 随着特征空间越来越大，Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧要靠工程师手工列出所有重要的交叉特征。
scenario_en: As the feature space grows, Wide & Deep's wide side needs engineers to hand-enumerate all important cross features.
q: Wide & Deep 的主要局限是什么？
q_en: What is Wide & Deep's main limitation?
why: wide 侧的记忆能力全靠人工构造的交叉特征——特征空间一大，工程师根本枚举不完所有有用组合，这成了特征工程瓶颈。DCN 正是为自动学交叉、绕开这个瓶颈而生。
why_en: The wide side's power depends on hand-crafted crosses, so as the space grows engineers can't enumerate all useful combinations, creating a feature-engineering bottleneck that DCN was built to remove.
options: wide 侧根本无法记忆任何特征共现，它是纯泛化模型
wide 侧记忆全靠人工交叉，特征一多枚举不完，成工程瓶颈
Wide & Deep 的两侧无法联合训练，必须分开训完再拼分数
它只吃稠密数值特征，处理不了高基数类别特征
options_en: The wide side cannot memorize any feature co-occurrence — it is a pure generalization model.
Wide-side memorization relies on manual crosses; once the feature space grows you can't enumerate them — a feature-engineering bottleneck.
The two sides of Wide & Deep can't be trained jointly; you must train them separately and stitch the scores.
It only takes dense numeric features and can't handle high-cardinality categorical features.
optionExplanations: wide 侧恰恰靠人工交叉做记忆，不是纯泛化。
对；人工枚举交叉在大特征空间不可行，正是 DCN 要自动化解决的瓶颈。
Wide&Deep 本来就是联合训练，这不是它的局限。
它处理类别特征（靠 embedding+交叉），不是只能稠密数值。
optionExplanations_en: The wide side memorizes via manual crosses — not pure generalization.
Correct — manual cross enumeration is infeasible in a large space, the bottleneck DCN automates.
Wide & Deep is jointly trained by design — not a limitation.
It handles categoricals (via embeddings + crosses), not only dense numerics.

termDefinitions.term: feature-engineering bottleneck / 特征工程瓶颈
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型能力依赖人工构造特征，特征空间增大后人力枚举跟不上，成为扩展瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature-engineering bottleneck is when model power depends on hand-crafted features that humans can't enumerate as the space grows.

scenario: 你不想再人工枚举交叉特征，希望模型自动学到特征之间的高阶交互，且不引发组合爆炸。
scenario_en: You want the model to learn feature interactions automatically without manual crosses or combinatorial explosion.
q: 该选哪种架构，它靠什么替代人工交叉？
q_en: Which architecture fits, and what replaces manual crosses?
why: 选 DCN：cross network 每层做 x_{l+1}=x0·x_l^T·w+b+x_l，随层数显式学多项式阶交互，不用手工枚举也不组合爆炸。deep 侧仍是普通 MLP。
why_en: Choose DCN: a cross network computes x_{l+1}=x0 x_l^T w + b + x_l per layer, learning explicit polynomial-order interactions without manual enumeration or explosion. The deep side stays a plain MLP.
tradeoff: DCN cross network（自动学交叉、低特征工程） vs Wide&Deep 人工交叉（要手工枚举、特征工程重）
options: 选 Wide & Deep，继续靠人工把更多有效的交叉特征一个个列举出来补齐
选 DCN：cross network 每层显式学多项式阶交互替代人工交叉，不组合爆炸
选纯线性回归，只要模型结构足够简单、参数足够少就够用了
选只做 embedding 查表、完全不建模任何特征之间交互关系的模型
options_en: Choose Wide & Deep, and keep hand-enumerating even more effective cross features one by one by hand to fill every gap.
Choose DCN: a cross network learns explicit polynomial interactions per layer, replacing manual crosses without explosion.
Choose pure linear regression, as long as the model stays simple with as few parameters as possible.
Choose a model that only does embedding lookups and models absolutely no interaction between any of the input features at all.
whenOtherWins: 如果你其实已经知道少数几个极强的交叉（如某垂类里 user×advertiser 就是决定性的），直接用 Wide & Deep 手工放进 wide 侧更简单直接，不必上 cross network。
whenOtherWins_en: If you already know a few dominant crosses (user x advertiser decisive in a vertical), placing them in Wide & Deep's wide side is simpler than a cross network.
optionExplanations: 人工列更多交叉正是要避免的特征工程瓶颈，这条路只会越走越窄。
对：显式多项式交互随层数自动生长，省掉了人工枚举那一步。
纯线性只能给一次线性组合，学不到特征之间的交互效应。
只查表没有交互步骤，会丢掉 CTR 最关键的特征共现信号。
optionExplanations_en: Enumerating more crosses by hand is exactly the feature-engineering trap this choice should avoid.
Correct — interaction depth grows layer by layer on its own, with no manual list-building required.
Pure linear only gives one linear combination and can't learn feature interactions at all.
Lookup-only skips the interaction step, dropping CTR's most important co-occurrence signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 cross network 自动学显式多项式特征交互（x_{l+1}=x0·x_l^T·w+b+x_l）替代人工交叉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep & Cross Network) uses a cross network to automatically learn explicit polynomial feature interactions, replacing manual crosses.

termDefinitions.meaning: DCN 的核心层，逐层做特征外积与残差，显式建模到层数的多项式交互，无组合爆炸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The cross network is DCN's core, applying feature outer products with residuals per layer to model polynomial interactions up to its depth without explosion.

scenario: DCN 的 cross layer 用一个向量权重 w，你想要更强的交互表达力。
scenario_en: DCN's cross layer uses a vector weight w, and you want more interaction expressiveness.
q: DCN-v2 相对原始 DCN 改了什么？
q_en: What does DCN-v2 change versus original DCN?
why: DCN-v2 把 cross layer 里的向量权重 w 换成矩阵 W：向量权重只能给每维一个标量缩放，矩阵能建模维度之间更丰富的交互组合，表达力更强，代价是参数更多。
why_en: DCN-v2 replaces the cross layer's vector weight w with a matrix W, so instead of a per-dimension scalar it models richer cross-dimension interactions with more expressiveness at the cost of more parameters.
options: 把向量权重 w 换成矩阵 W，建模更丰富的维度间交互，表达力更强
彻底删掉 cross network，只保留 deep 侧
把 deep 侧从 MLP 换成线性模型
去掉残差项，让每层不再累加 x_l
options_en: Replaces vector weight w with a matrix W for richer cross-dimension interactions and more expressiveness.
Removes the cross network entirely, keeping only the deep side.
Changes the deep side from an MLP to a linear model.
Drops the residual so layers no longer add x_l.
optionExplanations: 对；向量→矩阵权重让 cross layer 表达维度间更复杂的交互。
DCN-v2 强化的正是 cross network，不是删掉它。
deep 侧仍是 MLP，v2 改的是 cross layer 权重。
残差是 cross network 稳定训练的关键，v2 没去掉它。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — vector to matrix weight lets the cross layer express more complex cross-dimension interactions.
DCN-v2 strengthens the cross network, not removes it.
The deep side stays an MLP; v2 changes the cross-layer weight.
The residual is key to stable cross-network training; v2 keeps it.

termDefinitions.meaning: DCN 的改进版，把 cross layer 的向量权重 w 升级为矩阵 W，提升交互表达力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN-v2 upgrades DCN's cross-layer vector weight w to a matrix W for greater interaction expressiveness.

scenario: 面试官让你讲 DLRM（Meta 2019）的数据流：稀疏和稠密特征分别怎么走。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to trace DLRM's (Meta 2019) data flow for sparse and dense features.
q: DLRM 的结构和数据流是什么？
q_en: What is DLRM's structure and data flow?
why: DLRM：稠密走 bottom MLP，稀疏走 embedding 查表，两者 pairwise 点积后与 MLP 输出拼接进 top MLP。它为超大 embedding 表而生。
why_en: DLRM sends dense features through a bottom MLP and sparse features through embedding lookups, takes all pairwise dot-product interactions, concatenates with the bottom MLP, and passes through a top MLP.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["稠密特征"] --> B["bottom MLP"]
  S["稀疏特征"] --> L["embedding 查表"]
  B --> X["pairwise 点积交互"]
  L --> X
  X --> T["top MLP → pCTR"]
options: 稠密走 bottom MLP，稀疏查 embedding，点积交互后进 top MLP
稠密和稀疏 embedding 直接线性相加送进输出层，完全不做任何特征交互
只用稀疏 embedding 特征，稠密数值一律丢弃不进网络
稠密和稀疏各自训练一个独立模型，线上分数不做任何合并
options_en: Dense goes through a bottom MLP, sparse through embedding lookups, and the dot-product interactions feed a top MLP.
Dense and sparse embeddings are just summed linearly into the output layer with no feature interaction at all.
Only sparse embedding features are used; dense numerics are dropped before the network.
Dense and sparse each train a separate model and the online scores are never merged.
optionExplanations: 对；DLRM 的核心是稠密 MLP+稀疏 embedding+pairwise 点积交互，再过 top MLP。
线性相加学不到特征交互，不是 DLRM。
DLRM 稠密数值走 bottom MLP，不丢弃。
稠密和稀疏在交互层合并，不是各自独立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — DLRM's core is dense MLP + sparse embeddings + pairwise dot-product interactions, then a top MLP.
Linear summation learns no interactions — not DLRM.
DLRM sends dense numerics through the bottom MLP, not discarded.
Dense and sparse merge at the interaction layer, not independent.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 2019 架构，为超大 embedding 表设计：稠密走 MLP、稀疏走查表、pairwise 点积交互后过 top MLP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DLRM (Deep Learning Recommendation Model, Meta 2019) is built for massive embedding tables: dense via MLP, sparse via lookups, pairwise dot-product interactions, then a top MLP.

scenario: 你的 CTR 系统里 embedding 表大到几百 GB，装不进单张 GPU 显存。
scenario_en: Your CTR system's embedding tables are hundreds of GB, too big for one GPU.
q: 这种「embedding 表主导体量」的场景该选哪种架构，怎么服务？
q_en: For 'embedding tables dominate size', which architecture fits, and how to serve?
why: 选 DLRM：它就是为超大 embedding 表设计的，天然对应模型并行服务——把 embedding 表按 key 分片到多张 GPU，各存一部分、查表时并行取。当表到几百 GB、单卡放不下时，这是必需的部署形态。
why_en: Choose DLRM: built for massive embedding tables and mapping naturally to model-parallel serving, where tables are sharded across GPUs so each holds part and lookups run in parallel — necessary when tables reach hundreds of GB.
tradeoff: DLRM+模型并行（扛几百 GB embedding 表） vs 单卡稠密模型（表放不下、无法服务）
options: 选 Wide & Deep，人工交叉特征能把 embedding 表压小
选纯线性模型，不需要 embedding
选 DLRM+模型并行：embedding 表分片到多 GPU 并行查表
把整张 embedding 表塞进单张 GPU，加显存条就够了
options_en: Choose Wide & Deep — manual cross features shrink the embedding tables.
Choose a pure linear model that needs no embeddings.
Choose DLRM with model parallelism: shard the embedding tables across GPUs and look up in parallel.
Cram the whole embedding table into a single GPU; just add more VRAM.
whenOtherWins: 如果 embedding 表其实不大、能装进单卡，模型体量由别处主导，那用 DCN 等更简单的标准服务架构就够，不必上模型并行的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If embedding tables are small and fit one GPU, and size is dominated elsewhere, simpler standard-serving architectures like DCN suffice without model-parallel complexity.
optionExplanations: 人工交叉不能把几百 GB 的 embedding 表压小，答非所问。
纯线性没有 embedding 表达力，处理不了海量稀疏特征。
对；DLRM 对应模型并行，把大表分片到多 GPU，是几百 GB 表的标准部署。
几百 GB 超过单卡显存物理上限，加显存条也塞不下。
optionExplanations_en: Manual crosses can't shrink hundreds-of-GB embedding tables — misses the point.
Pure linear lacks embedding power and can't handle massive sparse features.
Correct — DLRM maps to model parallelism, sharding big tables across GPUs, the standard deployment for hundreds of GB.
Hundreds of GB exceed one GPU's physical VRAM; adding sticks won't fit it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个模型（这里是超大 embedding 表）分片到多张 GPU，各存一部分、并行计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model parallelism shards one model (here huge embedding tables) across GPUs, each holding part and computing in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存所有类别特征取值向量的大表，稀疏特征查表取向量，海量类别时可达几百 GB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table stores vectors for all categorical values; sparse features look up vectors, reaching hundreds of GB with huge cardinality.

scenario: 面试官让你横向比较 Wide&Deep、DCN、DLRM 在记忆、特征工程量、服务上的差异。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare Wide & Deep, DCN, and DLRM on memorization, feature-eng effort, and serving.
q: 三种 CTR 架构在特征工程量和服务上的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What are the core differences among the three CTR architectures on feature-eng effort and serving?
why: Wide&Deep 人工交叉→工程高；DCN 自动学交叉→工程低；DLRM 靠点积交互+超大表→工程中、需模型并行。选哪个看你有没有已知强交叉、表体量多大。
why_en: Wide&Deep's manual crosses mean high feature-eng, DCN's auto-learned crosses mean low, and DLRM's dot-product interactions with huge tables mean medium feature-eng but model-parallel serving.
options: 特征工程从高到低：Wide&Deep 人工交叉最重、DCN 自动学习最省；DLRM 大表需模型并行
三者的特征工程量和服务方式其实完全一样，选哪一个架构都无所谓没差别
说反了：DCN 特征工程量号称最高最麻烦，Wide&Deep 反而号称最低最省事、几乎不用调
三者不管选哪个，据说都需要模型并行服务，彼此完全没有区别可言
options_en: Feature-eng ranks high to low: Wide&Deep manual crosses heaviest, DCN auto-learning lightest; DLRM needs model parallelism for its huge tables.
All three actually have identical feature-eng effort and serving setup; it doesn't matter which one you pick at all.
Backwards: DCN's feature-eng is claimed to be highest and most work of the three, Wide&Deep supposedly the lowest and easiest by far.
All three, no matter which one you end up picking, are claimed to need model-parallel serving with absolutely zero difference between any of them.
optionExplanations: 对：这条从高到低的排序，正好把三个架构的选型依据串起来。
三者特征工程量和服务方式差别很大，绝不是随便选一个都行。
顺序反了：其实 Wide&Deep 的人工交叉才是工程量最重的一个，DCN 自动化后反而最省事。
只有 DLRM 因为大表才需要模型并行，Wide&Deep 和 DCN 标准服务即可。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this high-to-low ranking is exactly what ties the three architectures' selection logic together.
Their feature-eng effort and serving setup differ sharply — it's far from an arbitrary pick.
Order's flipped: Wide&Deep is the one that leans on hand-built feature crosses, DCN is the automated, lighter one.
Only DLRM's oversized tables push you toward sharding a model across GPUs; the other two serve in a standard setup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对所有特征向量两两做点积，显式建模每对特征的共现强度，DLRM 的交互方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pairwise interaction takes dot products between all feature-vector pairs to model each pair's co-occurrence, DLRM's interaction style.

tradeoff: 特征工程量 Wide&Deep(高) > DLRM(中) > DCN(低) vs 服务复杂度：只有 DLRM 因超大表需要模型并行
tradeoff_en: Feature-eng effort: Wide&Deep (high) > DLRM (medium) > DCN (low) vs serving complexity: only DLRM needs model parallelism, for its huge tables.

scenario: 某垂直广告里，user_id×advertiser_id 这几个交叉本身就是决定点击的强信号，团队也早知道这些交叉。
scenario_en: In a vertical, a few crosses like user_id x advertiser_id are themselves decisive click signals, already known to the team.
q: 已知少数强交叉的场景，最合适的架构是什么？
q_en: With a few known strong crosses, which architecture fits best?
why: 选 Wide & Deep：既然强交叉已知且数量不多，直接手工放进 wide 侧最直接——记忆强、实现简单，deep 侧补泛化。DCN 的自动学交叉在这里反而是杀鸡用牛刀。
why_en: Choose Wide & Deep: with a few known strong crosses, hand-placing them in the wide side is most direct — strong memorization, simple — while the deep side generalizes.
tradeoff: Wide&Deep（已知强交叉时最直接） vs DCN（交叉未知/太多时才值得自动学）
options: 选 DLRM，因为超大 embedding 表必须靠模型并行来服务
选 Wide & Deep：强交叉已知就手工放 wide 侧，deep 补泛化
选纯 deep MLP，让网络自己去学，忽略这几个已知强交叉
选纯线性模型，把交叉特征都塞进去，不要 deep 侧
options_en: Choose DLRM, because huge embedding tables have to be served with model parallelism.
Choose Wide & Deep: the strong crosses are known, so hand-place them on the wide side and let deep add generalization.
Choose a pure deep MLP and let the network figure it out, ignoring these known strong crosses.
Choose a pure linear model, stuff all crosses in, and drop the deep side.
whenOtherWins: 如果强交叉其实未知、或数量多到人工枚举不完，就该换 DCN 让 cross network 自动学，而不是硬塞 Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧。
whenOtherWins_en: If the strong crosses are unknown or too many to enumerate, switch to DCN's cross network instead of forcing them into Wide & Deep's wide side.
optionExplanations: 题里没说 embedding 表大到要模型并行，DLRM 不是这里的动机。
对；强交叉已知且少，手工放 wide 侧最直接高效，是 Wide&Deep 的强项。
纯 deep 会弱化对已知强交叉的记忆，浪费现成的强信号。
纯线性丢掉泛化能力，deep 侧的价值被扔掉了。
optionExplanations_en: The prompt doesn't say tables need model parallelism, so DLRM isn't the motive.
Correct — known, few strong crosses go directly into the wide side, Wide & Deep's strength.
Pure deep weakens memorization of known strong crosses, wasting a ready signal.
Pure linear drops generalization, throwing away the deep side's value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 领域先验里已确定对目标有强共现效应的特征组合，适合直接手工放进 wide 侧记忆。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A known cross is a feature combination whose strong co-occurrence effect is established by domain prior, ideal to hand-place in the wide side.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 的推荐模型：稠密走 bottom MLP、稀疏查 embedding，两者点积交互后进 top MLP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DLRM (Deep Learning Recommendation Model) sends dense features through a bottom MLP and sparse ones through embedding lookups, then combines them with dot-product interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把高基数类别特征（user_id、广告 id）映射成低维稠密向量，让模型能泛化到没见过的组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps a high-cardinality categorical feature such as a user id into a low-dimensional dense vector so the model can generalize to unseen combinations.

scenario: 广告拍卖按期望价值 = pCTR × bid 排序分配展示位。你的模型输出 0.05 时，必须真的对应 5% 的点击率。
scenario_en: Ad auctions rank by expected value = pCTR x bid; when your model outputs 0.05, it must truly mean a 5% click rate.
q: 为什么 CTR 模型的「校准」在拍卖里至关重要？
q_en: Why is CTR calibration critical in auctions?
why: 拍卖按 pCTR×bid 分钱，所以 pCTR 必须是真实概率：预测 0.05 就得对应真 5% 点击。对应关系一坏，钱就分错——过度自信让本不该赢的低质广告赢，信心不足让好广告被压。校准是让拍卖分配正确的前提。
why_en: Auctions allocate spend by pCTR x bid, so pCTR must be a true probability — 0.05 must mean a real 5% click rate — because broken correspondence misallocates spend: overconfidence lets low-quality ads win, underconfidence suppresses good ads.
tradeoff: 校准准（拍卖分配正确） vs 只排序对但不校准（pCTR×bid 分钱错位）
options: 拍卖只看 pCTR 排序，概率绝对值准不准与分钱无关
pCTR 必须是真实概率：高估让低质广告赢，低估压住好广告
校准只影响离线 AUC 这类指标，对线上收入没有影响
校准就是把所有 pCTR 都压到同一个常数上，比如 0.05
options_en: Auctions only look at pCTR ranking, so whether the absolute probability is right doesn't affect spend.
pCTR must be a true probability: overestimates let low-quality ads win, underestimates suppress good ads.
Calibration only affects offline metrics like AUC and has no impact on online revenue.
Calibration means squashing every pCTR to one constant, say 0.05.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统只需要「排出谁更可能被点」而从不用 pCTR 的绝对值分钱（如纯做相对排序展示），那校准就不关键，排序质量（AUC）才是重点。
whenOtherWins_en: If the system only ranks who's likelier to click and never uses pCTR's absolute value for spend, calibration isn't critical and ranking quality (AUC) is what matters.
optionExplanations: 拍卖用 pCTR 的绝对值乘 bid 分钱，不只是排序，校准直接决定分配。
对；pCTR 是拍卖里的真实概率，校准坏就系统性分错钱。
校准坏会直接扭曲 pCTR×bid 的线上分配，不只是离线指标。
校准是让 pCTR 对应真实点击率，不是把它压成常数。
optionExplanations_en: Auctions multiply pCTR's absolute value by bid to allocate — not just ranking; calibration decides allocation.
Correct — pCTR is a true probability in the auction, and miscalibration systematically misallocates spend.
Miscalibration directly distorts online pCTR x bid allocation, not just an offline metric.
Calibration makes pCTR match the true click rate, not flatten it to a constant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出的概率与真实频率一致：预测 0.05 就真有约 5% 点击，拍卖分钱的前提。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration means predicted probabilities match true frequencies — 0.05 really yields about 5% clicks — the prerequisite for auction spend allocation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告拍卖的期望价值排序键：预测点击率乘出价，pCTR 不准就分错钱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pCTR x bid is the auction's expected-value ranking key (predicted click rate times bid); a wrong pCTR misallocates spend.

scenario: 一个模型 AUC-ROC 很高，但把每个 pCTR 都系统性高估了一倍，团队却觉得「AUC 高就没问题」。
scenario_en: A model has high AUC-ROC but systematically doubles every pCTR, and the team thinks 'high AUC means fine'.
q: 为什么高 AUC 不代表校准好？两者分别衡量什么？
q_en: Why doesn't high AUC imply good calibration, and what does each measure?
why: AUC-ROC 衡量的是排序/区分能力（谁比谁更可能被点），完全不受校准影响——把所有 pCTR 乘 2，排序不变、AUC 不变，但概率全错。校准衡量的是「预测概率是否等于真实频率」。能分清区分 vs 校准，是生产意识的体现。
why_en: AUC-ROC measures ranking/discrimination (who's likelier than whom) and is unaffected by calibration — doubling all pCTRs keeps ranking and AUC identical while probabilities are all wrong — whereas calibration measures whether predicted probability equals true frequency.
tradeoff: AUC（区分/排序，无关校准） vs 校准（概率绝对值是否可信）
options: AUC 高就一定校准好，两个指标本质上是等价的
AUC 衡量排序、不受校准影响；校准衡量概率是否等于真实频率
反过来：校准衡量的是排序能力，AUC 衡量的是概率准确度
两者都只在离线评估里有用，上线后都不用再看
options_en: High AUC always means good calibration; the two metrics are essentially equivalent.
AUC measures ranking and is unaffected by calibration; calibration measures whether the probability equals the true frequency.
It's the other way round: calibration measures ranking ability and AUC measures probability accuracy.
Both only matter in offline evaluation and can be ignored once you're live.
optionExplanations: AUC 与校准正交：可以 AUC 完美却校准灾难，两者不等价。
对；AUC 只看排得对不对、校准看概率值准不准，一个模型可能前者好后者差。
说反了：AUC 衡量排序，校准衡量概率是否等于真实频率。
线上拍卖靠校准分钱、靠区分排序，二者线上都关键。
optionExplanations_en: AUC and calibration are orthogonal: perfect AUC can coexist with disastrous calibration — not equivalent.
Correct — AUC checks ordering, calibration checks probability values; a model can be good at one and bad at the other.
Backwards: AUC measures ranking, calibration whether probability equals true frequency.
Online auctions allocate by calibration and rank by discrimination; both matter online.

termDefinitions.fullName: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve
termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分类器排序/区分正负样本的能力，只看相对顺序，与概率校准无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC-ROC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures a classifier's ranking/discrimination ability from relative order only, independent of calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型把正样本排在负样本前面的能力，由 AUC 衡量，不涉及概率绝对值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Discrimination is the model's ability to rank positives above negatives, measured by AUC, independent of absolute probabilities.

scenario: 模型的错误校准是单调的（整体偏高或偏低），你想要一个几乎零延迟、好上线的后处理校准法。
scenario_en: The miscalibration is monotonic (overall too high or low), and you want a near-zero-latency, easy-to-ship post-hoc calibrator.
q: 该用哪种后处理校准方法，为什么？
q_en: Which post-hoc calibration method fits, and why?
why: 用 Platt scaling：在留出集上对原始 logits 拟合一个逻辑回归 p_cal=σ(A·z+B)。它适合单调错误校准，只多一次 sigmoid、延迟几乎为零，是默认选择。非单调的复杂偏差它救不了，那才轮到 isotonic。
why_en: Use Platt scaling: fit a logistic regression on raw logits, p_cal=σ(A·z+B), on a held-out set — good for monotonic miscalibration with just one sigmoid at negligible latency, the default.
tradeoff: Platt scaling（单调偏差、零延迟、默认） vs isotonic（能修非单调但要更多数据+查表）
options: 用 isotonic regression，非参数最灵活，什么偏差都能拟合
用 Platt scaling：在 logits 上拟合 σ(A·z+B)，延迟近零
重新训练整个模型来修校准，不做任何后处理
把所有 pCTR 手动乘一个固定系数，比如统一减半
options_en: Use isotonic regression — non-parametric and most flexible, it can fit any kind of bias.
Use Platt scaling: fit σ(A·z+B) on the logits, adding almost no latency.
Retrain the whole model to fix calibration instead of doing any post-processing.
Multiply every pCTR by a fixed constant by hand, for example halving them all.
whenOtherWins: 如果错误校准是非单调的（有的区间偏高有的偏低），Platt 的单调逻辑形拟合不了，这时才该换 isotonic regression。
whenOtherWins_en: If the miscalibration is non-monotonic (some ranges too high, others too low), Platt's monotonic logistic form can't fit it, and you switch to isotonic regression.
optionExplanations: isotonic 更灵活但要更多数据+查表，单调偏差场景是杀鸡用牛刀。
对；Platt 拟合一次逻辑回归、零延迟，正好治单调偏差，是默认后处理校准。
重训整模型成本高、慢，后处理校准就是为避免这个。
手动减半是拍脑袋，救不了不同区间的不同偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Isotonic is more flexible but needs more data + a lookup — overkill for monotonic miscalibration.
Correct — Platt fits one logistic regression at zero latency, ideal for monotonic bias, the default post-hoc calibrator.
Retraining the whole model is costly and slow — post-hoc calibration exists to avoid it.
Manual halving is arbitrary and can't fix different biases in different ranges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后处理校准：在留出集上对原始 logits 拟合逻辑回归 σ(A·z+B)，适合单调偏差、延迟极低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling is post-hoc calibration fitting a logistic regression σ(A·z+B) on raw logits, good for monotonic bias at very low latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过 sigmoid 之前的原始分数 z，Platt 在它上面拟合校准函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A logit is the raw pre-sigmoid score z on which Platt fits its calibration function.

scenario: 校准曲线显示错误是非单调的：低分区间预测偏低、中分区间又偏高，Platt 的单调逻辑形拟合不了。
scenario_en: The calibration curve is non-monotonic: underpredicting at low scores, overpredicting mid-range, which Platt's monotonic form can't fit.
q: 这种非单调偏差该用什么校准法，代价是什么？
q_en: For non-monotonic bias, which calibrator fits, and at what cost?
why: 用 isotonic regression：非参数的单调阶梯函数，能拟合 Platt 拟合不了的非单调/复杂偏差模式。代价是要更多数据（否则过拟合阶梯），且服务时要维护一个查表映射，比 Platt 一次 sigmoid 重。
why_en: Use isotonic regression: a non-parametric monotonic step function that fits complex/non-monotonic patterns Platt can't, at the cost of needing more data and a serving-time lookup table.
tradeoff: isotonic（拟合复杂偏差但要更多数据+查表） vs Platt（简单零延迟但只治单调）
options: 继续用 Platt，把逻辑回归多拟合几轮就能覆盖非单调
用 isotonic regression：非参数阶梯拟合复杂偏差
放弃校准，反正 AUC 高说明排序已经对了
把非单调区间的样本全删掉，只留能被 Platt 拟合的部分
options_en: Stick with Platt — just refit the logistic regression a few more rounds and it will cover non-monotonic bias.
Use isotonic regression: a non-parametric step function that fits complex bias.
Give up on calibration, since a high AUC means the ranking is already right.
Delete every sample in the non-monotonic range and keep only what Platt can fit.
whenOtherWins: 如果偏差其实是单调的、或数据量不足以稳住阶梯函数，就该退回 Platt scaling——它更省数据、零延迟。
whenOtherWins_en: If the bias is actually monotonic or data is too scarce to stabilize the step function, fall back to Platt scaling — cheaper on data, zero latency.
optionExplanations: Platt 是单调逻辑形，多拟合几次也拟合不了非单调偏差。
对；isotonic 非参数阶梯能治非单调，代价是更吃数据、需查表。
AUC 高不代表概率准，拍卖仍会因校准差分错钱。
删样本掩盖问题、丢信息，不能真正校准。
optionExplanations_en: Platt is a monotonic logistic form; refitting can't fix non-monotonic bias.
Correct — isotonic's non-parametric step fixes non-monotonic bias, at more data and a lookup cost.
High AUC doesn't mean accurate probabilities; the auction still misallocates from bad calibration.
Deleting samples hides the problem and loses info, not real calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非参数单调阶梯函数校准，能拟合非单调复杂偏差，需更多数据并在服务时查表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isotonic regression is a non-parametric monotonic step-function calibrator that fits complex non-monotonic bias, needing more data and a serving lookup.

scenario: 面试官让你并排比较 Platt scaling 和 isotonic regression 的适用偏差、数据需求、服务开销。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare Platt scaling and isotonic regression on bias type, data need, and serving cost.
q: Platt 和 isotonic 两种校准法怎么对比？
q_en: How do Platt and isotonic calibration contrast?
why: Platt 是参数化逻辑回归，只治单调偏差、几乎不需额外数据、延迟一次 sigmoid，是默认；isotonic 非参数阶梯，能治非单调偏差、需更多数据防过拟合、服务时查表更重。轴是「偏差复杂度 vs 数据/延迟成本」。
why_en: Platt is a parametric logistic fit for monotonic bias needing little data at one-sigmoid latency (default), while isotonic is a non-parametric step for non-monotonic bias needing more data and a lookup.
options: 两者适用的偏差类型和服务成本完全一样，可以随便换
Platt 参数化治单调、省数据、零延迟；isotonic 治非单调但更重
反过来：Platt 治非单调偏差，isotonic 只治单调偏差
两者都要重新训练模型，属于训练期方法而非后处理
options_en: Their applicable bias types and serving costs are identical, so you can swap them freely.
Platt is parametric, fixes monotonic bias, is data-light and near zero latency; isotonic fixes non-monotonic bias but is heavier.
The other way round: Platt fixes non-monotonic bias and isotonic only fixes monotonic bias.
Both require retraining the model, making them training-time methods rather than post-processing.
optionExplanations: 两者适用偏差和成本差别明显，不是一样。
对；参数 vs 非参数、单调 vs 非单调、省数据零延迟 vs 吃数据查表，正好切开二者。
说反了：Platt 治单调、isotonic 治非单调。
两者都是后处理校准、不重训模型。
optionExplanations_en: Their bias types and costs differ clearly — not identical.
Correct — parametric vs non-parametric, monotonic vs non-monotonic, data-light/zero-latency vs data-hungry/lookup cleanly split them.
Backwards: Platt fixes monotonic, isotonic non-monotonic.
Both are post-hoc calibration without retraining the model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后在原始输出上再拟合一个校准函数，不改主模型，如 Platt/isotonic。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Post-hoc calibration fits a calibration function on the trained model's outputs without changing it, e.g. Platt/isotonic.

scenario: 上线时模型校准得很好，但几周后随着用户行为和广告库变化，pCTR 又逐渐偏离真实点击率。
scenario_en: The model was well-calibrated at launch, but weeks later pCTR drifts from true click rate as behavior and inventory change.
q: 校准会随时间漂移，该怎么办？
q_en: Calibration drifts over time — what should you do?
why: 校准不是一次性的：分布随时间变（用户行为、广告库更新），pCTR 会逐渐失准，拍卖又开始分错钱。所以要持续监控校准（如可靠性曲线偏离对角线的程度），发现漂移就重新拟合校准层或重训。
why_en: Calibration isn't one-and-done: as distributions shift, pCTR drifts and the auction misallocates again, so monitor calibration continuously and refit the calibrator or retrain when drift appears.
options: 校准一次就永久有效，之后不用再管，模型自己会跟上
分布随时间漂移→pCTR 逐渐失准；持续监控，漂了就重拟合校准层
漂移只影响离线 AUC 这类指标，拍卖分钱不受影响
把 pCTR 固定成上线时的值，输出不再随模型变化就不会漂
options_en: Calibrate once and it holds forever; the model keeps up on its own.
Distributions drift so pCTR slowly goes off; monitor calibration and refit the calibration layer when it drifts.
Drift only affects offline metrics like AUC and doesn't change how the auction allocates spend.
Freeze pCTR at its launch values so the output stops moving with the model.
optionExplanations: 分布会变，校准会随之退化，绝非一劳永逸。
对；漂移让 pCTR 再次失真、拍卖分错钱，需持续监控+定期重拟合校准。
漂移直接影响概率绝对值→pCTR×bid 分配，不只是 AUC。
冻结 pCTR 会让它彻底脱离真实点击率，漂得更离谱。
optionExplanations_en: Distributions change and calibration degrades — not one-and-done.
Correct — drift re-distorts pCTR and misallocates spend, so monitor continuously and periodically refit the calibrator.
Drift affects absolute probabilities and thus pCTR x bid allocation, not just AUC.
Freezing pCTR detaches it from the true click rate, drifting worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布随时间变化导致 pCTR 逐渐偏离真实点击率，需持续监控与重新校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration drift is pCTR gradually deviating from the true click rate as distributions change, needing continuous monitoring and recalibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率 vs 观测频率的曲线，完美校准时落在对角线，偏离即失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reliability curve plots predicted probability vs observed frequency; perfect calibration lies on the diagonal, deviation means miscalibration.

scenario: 只预测 CTR 会忽略转化(CVR)和长期价值(LTV)，但这些对广告业务同样重要。
scenario_en: Predicting only CTR ignores conversions (CVR) and lifetime value (LTV), which matter to the ad business too.
q: 怎么用一个模型同时建模 CTR、CVR、LTV？
q_en: How do you model CTR, CVR, and LTV in one model?
why: 用共享底座 + 任务专属塔：共享 embedding+MLP 学到用户-广告的共同表示，再分出 CTR、CVR、LTV 各自的塔 MLP。相关任务共享底层表示互相受益，又各留一个头输出各自预测。
why_en: Use a shared-bottom plus task-specific towers: shared embeddings + MLP learn a common user-ad representation, then separate tower MLPs for CTR, CVR, and LTV.
tradeoff: 共享底座+多塔（相关任务互益、省算力） vs 每任务独立模型（零干扰但重复底座、丢共享）
options: 给 CTR、CVR、LTV 三个目标各自训一个完全独立、互不共享参数的模型
共享底座+任务专属塔：共享 embedding+MLP 学共同表示，再分各自塔 MLP
只训 CTR 这一个目标，CVR 和 LTV 全靠人工规则拍脑袋去估算
把三个目标的数值直接加起来当成一个标量，拿去做单目标回归
options_en: Train three fully separate models for CTR, CVR, and LTV that share no parameters with each other at all.
Shared-bottom + task towers: shared embeddings + MLP learn a common representation, then separate tower MLPs.
Train only the CTR objective, and guess CVR and LTV purely by hand-rolled rules of thumb.
Sum the three objectives' values into a single scalar and regress that one number directly.
whenOtherWins: 如果 CTR、CVR、LTV 之间几乎没有共享信号、甚至相互冲突严重，强行共享底座会互相污染，这时分开独立模型反而更稳。
whenOtherWins_en: If CTR/CVR/LTV share little signal or conflict heavily, a forced shared bottom pollutes them, and separate models are more stable.
optionExplanations: 独立模型各自从零学一遍底座，丢掉了任务间可迁移的共同信号——这份信号在相关任务里本该是免费的增益。
对；共享底座学共同表示、各塔出各任务预测，是 CTR 多任务标准解。
拍脑袋规则给不出可优化的 CVR/LTV，浪费可学信号。
三目标加成一个标量会糊掉各自语义，无法分别校准/使用。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models relearn the bottom from scratch for each task, discarding the shared signal that related tasks could otherwise reuse for free.
Correct — a shared bottom learns the common representation and towers output per-task predictions, the standard CTR multi-task solution.
Rule-guessing gives no optimizable CVR/LTV, wasting learnable signal.
Summing three into one scalar blurs their semantics, preventing separate calibration/use.

termDefinitions.meaning: 转化率：点击后完成目标动作（购买/注册）的比例，比点击更接近商业价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CVR (Conversion Rate) is the fraction of clicks that complete a target action (purchase/signup), closer to business value than clicks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户/转化的长期价值，标签延迟数天到数周才成熟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LTV (Lifetime Value) is the long-term value of a user/conversion, with labels maturing days to weeks later.

scenario: CTR/CVR/LTV 合成损失 L=w_ctr·L_ctr+w_cvr·L_cvr+w_ltv·L_ltv，三个任务收敛速度还不一样。
scenario_en: The combined loss L=w_ctr·L_ctr+w_cvr·L_cvr+w_ltv·L_ltv, with tasks converging at different rates.
q: 这三个任务权重该怎么设？
q_en: How should the three task weights be set?
why: 静态固定权重不理想——任务收敛速度不同，固定比例跟不上。用不确定性加权：让模型按每个任务的（学习到的）不确定性自动下调噪声大/不确定的任务，自动平衡各任务影响，比手调固定权重更稳。
why_en: Static fixed weights are suboptimal since tasks converge at different rates, so use uncertainty weighting to auto-downweight high-uncertainty (noisy) tasks and balance influence automatically.
tradeoff: 不确定性加权（自动平衡、跟随收敛速度） vs 静态固定权重（简单但跟不上不同收敛速率）
options: 静态固定权重最好，调一次上线后永远不用再改
用不确定性加权：按学到的任务不确定性自动下调噪声大的任务
三个权重恒等于 1，让三个任务的梯度完全平等
只保留 CTR 的权重，CVR/LTV 两个任务权重设 0
options_en: Static fixed weights are best — tune once at launch and never touch them again.
Use uncertainty weighting: automatically down-weight noisy tasks by their learned uncertainty.
Keep all three weights at 1 so every task's gradient counts equally.
Keep only the CTR weight and set the CVR and LTV weights to 0.
whenOtherWins: 如果三个任务噪声水平相近、且你已经手调出一组好用的固定权重，静态权重更简单，不必引入可学习不确定性的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the three tasks have similar noise and you've hand-tuned good fixed weights, static weighting is simpler than learnable uncertainty.
optionExplanations: 静态权重跟不上不同收敛速率，一般是次优。
对；不确定性加权自动压噪声任务、随训练平衡各任务，比手调更稳。
恒等权重忽略任务噪声/收敛差异，易让某任务主导。
只留 CTR 就放弃了 CVR/LTV 的多任务收益，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Static weights can't track differing convergence rates and are generally suboptimal.
Correct — uncertainty weighting auto-suppresses noisy tasks and balances across training, steadier than hand-tuning.
Equal weights ignore noise/convergence differences, letting a task dominate.
Keeping only CTR abandons the CVR/LTV multi-task benefit, missing the point.

termDefinitions.term: uncertainty weighting / 不确定性加权
termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个任务学习到的不确定性自动加权损失，噪声大的任务权重自动降低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Uncertainty weighting auto-weights each task's loss by its learned uncertainty, lowering the weight of noisier tasks.

scenario: 转化(CVR)标签很稀有（点击里只有少数会转化），LTV 标签要几天到几周后才成熟。
scenario_en: Conversion (CVR) labels are rare (few clicks convert), and LTV labels only mature days to weeks later.
q: 标签稀疏+延迟反馈会带来什么问题，怎么缓解？
q_en: What problem do label sparsity + delayed feedback cause, and how to mitigate?
why: 转化稀有 + LTV 延迟成熟 → 严重的类别不平衡和标签滞后，稀疏任务学不动。缓解：用重要性采样上调稀有转化样本的权重；把点击当辅助任务，给共享层灌入密集梯度信号，托住 CVR/LTV 这些稀疏任务。
why_en: Rare conversions + delayed LTV cause severe imbalance and label lag so sparse tasks barely learn — mitigated by importance sampling to upweight rare conversions and using clicks as an auxiliary task to give dense gradient to shared layers.
options: 没什么问题，稀疏标签一样能把 CVR/LTV 训到收敛
严重不平衡+标签滞后→稀疏任务学不动；重要性采样+点击做辅助任务
只是训练变慢一点，多加机器加大 batch 就能解决
把稀有的转化样本直接删掉，让训练数据分布更干净
options_en: No real problem — sparse labels still train CVR and LTV to convergence.
Severe imbalance plus label lag stalls the sparse tasks; importance-sample rare conversions and use clicks as an auxiliary task.
It's only somewhat slower training; add machines and a bigger batch and it's fixed.
Just delete the rare conversion samples to make the training distribution cleaner.
optionExplanations: 稀有+延迟标签让 CVR/LTV 信号太弱，学不好，不是没问题。
对；重要性采样补稀有转化权重、点击辅助任务给密集梯度，正好托住稀疏任务。
这不是速度问题，是信号稀疏导致学不动，加机器无用。
删稀有转化正好抹掉最宝贵的正样本，让 CVR 更学不到。
optionExplanations_en: Rare + delayed labels make CVR/LTV signal too weak to learn well — not fine.
Correct — importance sampling upweights rare conversions and clicks as auxiliary give dense gradient, propping up sparse tasks.
It's not speed but sparse signal blocking learning; machines don't help.
Deleting rare conversions erases the most valuable positives, worsening CVR learning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对稀有类样本（转化）在损失里上调权重，抵消类别不平衡带来的学习不足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Importance sampling upweights rare-class samples (conversions) in the loss to offset class imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签要过一段时间才成熟（LTV 数天到数周），训练时真值暂不可得。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed feedback is when labels mature only after a delay (LTV days to weeks), so ground truth isn't available at training time.

scenario: CVR 塔因为转化标签太稀疏，共享底座从它那儿几乎收不到有用梯度。
scenario_en: The CVR tower gets almost no useful gradient to the shared bottom because conversion labels are so sparse.
q: 为什么「把点击当辅助任务」能帮到稀疏的 CVR/LTV？
q_en: Why does 'clicks as an auxiliary task' help sparse CVR/LTV?
why: 点击标签又多又密集，把点击当辅助任务能给共享底座灌入大量梯度信号，把共同的用户-广告表示学扎实；CVR/LTV 虽稀疏，但共享了这个学好的底座，就能在少量标签上也学得更稳。辅助任务是给主稀疏任务托底。
why_en: Click labels are abundant and dense, so using clicks as an auxiliary task feeds strong gradient into the shared bottom, learning a solid user-ad representation that sparse CVR/LTV then reuse, learning better on few labels.
tradeoff: 点击辅助任务（密集梯度托底共享层） vs 只训稀疏 CVR/LTV（共享底座梯度不足、学不动）
options: 点击和转化完全无关，加它纯粹是凑一个辅助任务
点击标签密集，给共享底座灌梯度学好表示，CVR/LTV 复用它
点击辅助任务会直接替代 CVR 塔，之后不用再训 CVR
因为它能把稀疏的 CVR 标签数量直接变多
options_en: Clicks and conversions are unrelated, so it's just an auxiliary task for the sake of it.
Click labels are dense, feeding gradient into the shared bottom to learn a good representation that CVR and LTV reuse.
The click auxiliary task simply replaces the CVR tower, so you don't need to train CVR anymore.
Because it literally increases the number of sparse CVR labels.
whenOtherWins: 如果点击和转化的用户-广告表示其实相差很大（辅助信号与主任务不相关），点击辅助反而会把共享底座带偏，这时不该用它托底。
whenOtherWins_en: If click and conversion representations differ a lot (auxiliary signal unrelated), clicks as auxiliary can skew the shared bottom and shouldn't be used.
optionExplanations: 点击和转化共享用户-广告表示，高度相关，不是凑数。
对；密集点击梯度先把共享底座学好，稀疏 CVR/LTV 复用它就学得更稳。
辅助任务是托底不是替代，CVR 仍要有自己的塔和训练。
辅助任务不凭空造 CVR 标签，它靠共享表示间接帮忙。
optionExplanations_en: Clicks and conversions share the user-ad representation, highly related, not filler.
Correct — dense click gradient first builds a solid shared bottom that sparse CVR/LTV reuse to learn steadily.
The auxiliary props up, not replaces; CVR still needs its own tower and training.
The auxiliary doesn't fabricate CVR labels; it helps indirectly via shared representation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签密集的次要任务（点击），用其密集梯度把共享表示学扎实，托底稀疏的主任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auxiliary task is a label-dense secondary task (clicks) whose dense gradient strengthens the shared representation to prop up sparse main tasks.

scenario: 多任务上线后，广告排序不再只用 pCTR×bid，而是把转化和长期价值也算进去。
scenario_en: With multi-task live, ad ranking no longer uses just pCTR x bid but folds in conversion and long-term value.
q: 服务打分公式 pCTR×pCVR×bid×f(LTV) 各项在设计上表达什么？
q_en: What does each term in the serving score pCTR x pCVR x bid x f(LTV) express?
why: 服务分 = pCTR×pCVR×bid×f(LTV)：分别是点击概率、转化概率、出价与长期价值权重的乘积。它取代简单的 pCTR×bid，让拍卖对齐真实转化与长期价值。
why_en: The serving score pCTR x pCVR x bid x f(LTV) multiplies click probability, conversion probability, bid, and a long-term-value weight, replacing plain pCTR x bid to align the auction with real conversions and value.
options: 这是死记硬背的固定公式，背下每一项才是考点，不用理解含义
pCTR×pCVR×bid×f(LTV)：对应点击、转化、出价与长期价值权重
只要 pCTR 一项就够用，pCVR、bid、f(LTV) 三项都可以直接删掉
各项都只是记录用的日志字段，跟拍卖怎么分配展示位置完全无关
options_en: It's a fixed formula to memorize term by term, without needing to understand it.
pCTR x pCVR x bid x f(LTV): maps to click, conversion, bid, and long-term-value weight.
Only pCTR matters; pCVR, bid, and f(LTV) can all be dropped.
Every term is just a logging field, unrelated to how the auction allocates ad slots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测的点击后转化概率，进服务打分对齐真实转化而非只看点击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pCVR (predicted Conversion Rate) is the model's post-click conversion probability, in the serving score to align with real conversions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测长期价值折算成打分权重的函数，让拍卖偏向长期有价值的广告。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: f(LTV) is a platform value function converting predicted long-term value into a scoring weight, biasing the auction toward valuable ads.

optionExplanations: 死记公式拿不到设计分：面试要答的是每项对应哪个业务目标，不是背等式本身。
对：四项分别锁定点击、转化、出价与长期价值权重，缺一项就丢一块商业目标。
只留 pCTR 会丢掉转化和长期价值两个目标，拍卖又退回旧问题。
这几项直接乘进打分决定谁赢拍卖，不是可以忽略的日志字段。
optionExplanations_en: Rote memorizing the equation misses the point — interviewers want what each term maps to, not the formula itself.
Correct — each factor pulls in a different success signal, so losing any one breaks part of the auction's incentive.
Keeping only pCTR drops conversion and long-term value, sliding the auction back to the old problem.
These four terms multiply directly into the score that picks the auction's winner, not sidelined logging.

scenario: 一个未校准的 CTR 模型上线到 pCTR×bid 的拍卖里，它对某些广告系统性高估了点击率。
scenario_en: An uncalibrated CTR model goes live in a pCTR x bid auction and systematically overestimates some ads' click rates.
q: 未校准模型在 pCTR×bid 拍卖里的核心风险是什么？
q_en: What's the core risk of an uncalibrated model in a pCTR x bid auction?
why: 被高估 CTR 的广告会赢下它们本不该赢的拍卖：pCTR 虚高→pCTR×bid 虚高→挤掉真正更该展示的广告，扭曲收入分配、伤广告主和用户体验。这正是校准在拍卖里不可省的原因。
why_en: Ads with overestimated CTR win auctions they shouldn't — inflated pCTR inflates pCTR x bid, crowding out ads that deserve the slot — distorting revenue allocation and hurting advertisers and UX.
options: 没有风险，只要相对排序对了，绝对概率偏不偏都无所谓
被高估的广告赢下本不该赢的拍卖，挤掉更该展示的广告
只会让推理延迟变高，和拍卖怎么分钱没有关系
会让所有广告都低于底价而不展示，拍卖直接失效
options_en: No risk — as long as the relative ranking is right, absolute probability error doesn't matter.
Ads with overestimated CTR win auctions they shouldn't, crowding out ads that deserved the slot.
It only raises inference latency and has nothing to do with how the auction splits spend.
It pushes every ad below the reserve price so nothing shows and the auction breaks.
optionExplanations: 拍卖靠 pCTR 绝对值乘 bid 分钱，只排对顺序不够，校准坏就分错。
对；高估 CTR 抬高 pCTR×bid，让不该赢的广告赢，系统性扭曲分配。
这是收入分配扭曲问题，不是延迟问题。
未校准是分配扭曲，不是全部不展示，拍卖仍在跑只是分错。
optionExplanations_en: Auctions allocate by pCTR's absolute value times bid, so right order isn't enough — bad calibration misallocates.
Correct — overestimated CTR inflates pCTR x bid so undeserving ads win, systematically distorting allocation.
It's a revenue-allocation distortion, not a latency issue.
Uncalibration distorts allocation, not shows nothing; the auction still runs but misallocates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拍卖按 pCTR×bid 决定哪个广告拿到展示位、平台赚多少，pCTR 失准就分配错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Revenue allocation is how the auction decides which ad wins the slot and platform revenue via pCTR x bid; a wrong pCTR misallocates it.

q: 补全 CTR 模型设计的核心张力与三决策：
q_en: Fill in CTR model design's core tension and three decisions:
text: 核心张力是 {{记忆}}（记住 user×advertiser 共现）vs {{泛化}}（预测没见过的组合）。三个关键决策：{{架构}}（Wide&Deep/DCN/DLRM）、{{校准}}（pCTR 要等于真实点击率）、{{多任务}}（CTR/CVR/LTV 联合）。
text_en: The core tension is {{memorization}} (recall user x advertiser co-occurrence) vs {{generalization}} (predict unseen combos). Three decisions: {{architecture}} (Wide&Deep/DCN/DLRM), {{calibration}} (pCTR must equal the true click rate), {{multi-task}} (joint CTR/CVR/LTV).
why: 记住这张地图：记忆 vs 泛化是主轴，架构选哪个模型、校准保证 pCTR 可用于拍卖、多任务把 CVR/LTV 也纳入优化。三决策各解一层。
why_en: The map: memorization vs generalization is the axis, architecture picks the model, calibration makes pCTR auction-usable, and multi-task folds in CVR/LTV.

scenario: 面试官想确认你理解记忆和泛化分别对应模型的哪部分、各擅长什么。
scenario_en: The interviewer checks you understand which model parts do memorization vs generalization and what each is good at.
q: 记忆和泛化各由模型哪部分承担，分别擅长什么？
q_en: Which model parts do memorization and generalization, and what is each good at?
why: 记忆由 wide/交叉侧承担：记高频共现、对头部准。泛化由 deep/embedding 侧承担：靠稠密向量覆盖长尾新组合。
why_en: Memorization is the wide/cross side recalling frequent feature co-occurrences (seen strong combos like user x advertiser), accurate on head samples, while generalization is the deep/embedding side compressing sparse features into dense vectors to predict unseen long-tail combos.
tradeoff: 记忆（wide/交叉，头部共现准） vs 泛化（deep/embedding，长尾新组合可预测）
options: 记忆和泛化都由同一个线性层承担，模型内部没有分工
记忆=wide/交叉侧记高频共现；泛化=deep 侧覆盖长尾新组合
反过来：记忆由 deep 侧承担，泛化由 wide 交叉侧承担
两者只影响训练收敛速度，和线上预测能力没有关系
options_en: One linear layer handles both memorization and generalization with no division of labor.
Memorization is the wide/cross side recalling frequent co-occurrences; generalization is the deep side covering long-tail new combos.
The other way round: memorization comes from the deep side and generalization from the wide cross side.
Both only affect how fast training converges and say nothing about online prediction quality.
optionExplanations: 记忆和泛化分属不同结构（交叉 vs embedding），不是同一层。
对；两端分工明确，工程上也是两条不同的特征通道。
方向反了：手工交叉走线性那一侧，稠密向量走神经网络那一侧。
这是预测能力的分工，不是训练速度问题。
optionExplanations_en: Memorization and generalization live in different structures (cross vs embedding), not one layer.
Correct — the split is clean, and in practice they are two separate feature pathways.
Reversed: manual crosses live on the linear side and dense vectors on the neural-network side.
It's a prediction-capability division, not a training-speed issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出现次数很少的特征组合，靠记忆学不到、需泛化侧的 embedding 给合理预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The long tail is rarely-occurring feature combinations that memorization can't learn, needing the generalization side's embeddings.
